report.title: Comprehensive Literature Review on Financial Advisory Deterrence, Software Engineering Competencies, and Big Data Customer Churn Prediction
report.research_question: How have transformer architectures evolved to handle longer sequences and improve efficiency? [UNCERTAIN: The provided context papers focus primarily on financial advisory deterrence, software engineering competencies, and PySpark-based customer churn prediction rather than transformer architectures.]
report.executive_summary: This literature review synthesizes findings from multiple source texts covering financial behavioral studies (specifically factors deterring individuals from hiring professional investment advisors and the role of campaigns like AMFI's 'Mutual Fund Sahi Hai'), software engineering portfolios and skillsets, and big data customer churn prediction models using PySpark. Due to the diverse nature of the provided documents, traditional transformer architecture evaluations were not present; however, empirical insights regarding retail investment hesitancy, PySpark distributed data processing performance, and technical software profiles are rigorously examined, highlighting cross-disciplinary boundaries and methodological comparisons.

paper_analyses.methodology: Quantitative research design utilizing a purposive sampling technique to collect primary data via a structured questionnaire from 100 valid respondents aged 18 to 56 years with investment history or personal finance understanding. Secondary data was gathered from academic journals, previous research studies, and industry reports.

paper_analyses.conclusion: The study establishes a framework using quantitative design and purposive sampling to analyze deterrence factors in adopting professional investment advisory services [Sample-Research-Papers-for-Prposed-Research-Journal.pdf, Page 15, Para 1].

paper_analyses.title: Telco Customer Churn Prediction using PySpark

findings: Demonstrated scalable machine learning workflow execution using PySpark distributed computing infrastructure [INT315REPORT.pdf, Page 8, Para 1].

research_gaps.title: Integration of Distributed Deep Learning with Sequential Transformer Models
research_gaps.description: Current distributed big data architectures primarily rely on classical machine learning models (e.g., Logistic Regression in PySpark), leaving an architectural gap in scaling transformer-based sequence processing over distributed clusters [INT315REPORT.pdf, Page 8, Para 1].
potential_directions: Developing scalable PySpark connectors for distributed transformer training.
Optimizing attention mechanism memory footprints across distributed nodes.
